chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Asadi al-Kufi narrated, on the authority of Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, on the authority of his paternal uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, on the authority of Ali ibn Salm, on the authority of Abu Basir, on the authority of Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (AS) who said:

Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, cannot be described in terms of time, space, motion, translocation or stillness. Rather, He is the Creator of time, space, motion and stillness. Exalted is Allah from what they say, the Elevated, the Great.
ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology describe Allah's relationship with time and space?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the Shia doctrine of divine transcendence (tanzih) by negating physical limitations like time, space, and motion, affirming Allah as their Creator rather than being subject to them. It reflects the theological debates against anthropomorphists (mujassima) who attributed bodily characteristics to God, establishing a clear metaphysical distinction between the Creator and creation. The concluding verse underscores this absolute purity, reinforcing that human descriptions fall short of His true essence.
